text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has fallen nearly 16% over two weeks, with today's modest decline of about 1% occurring after a sharp 9% drop yesterday. The timing and magnitude of this collapse align with the post-election political shift: news on November 5th revealed that Democrats will investigate Trump-era energy deals and policies, including interventions in Venezuela and mineral arrangements. For a refiner like Marathon, this creates near-term uncertainty about regulatory treatment and energy policy direction, especially given Democratic interest in supporting renewables over fossil fuels.

The broader context makes the selloff understandable: refinery operations are running hot at 94.5%, but crude oil prices have pulled back sharply (US oil at $99.64 per barrel from higher levels earlier in the week), which typically squeezes refiner margins. Political risk compounds a sector already facing headwinds from policy uncertainty and the transition away from traditional energy sources.
